plan.angle:
Minimum-effort carousel built only from the verified 10-25 bones Short script, with no new research. Drop it if that script isn't confirmed as verified.

Slides:
(1) The worry, named as understandable.
(2) 8 small randomized trials in adults with overweight or obesity, mostly exenatide and liraglutide, one semaglutide trial, no tirzepatide. Use the n exactly as verified.
(3) Very low certainty: too thin to tell whether these drugs help, spare or harm bone, and fracture trials are needed.
(4) Losing weight by any method can come with some bone loss.
(5) Recommended habits, not proven on the drug: muscle-strengthening at least 2 days a week, started gently, and a protein food at each meal unless your clinician has told you to limit protein.
(6) If you have osteoporosis or fracture risk, ask your clinician about bone health. Common GI side effects. 'Don't stop or change your medicines on your own.'
(7) 'Not personal advice' plus the full prescriber line.

No emoji, no scare visuals, no #Tirzepatide.

package.title: Do GLP-1 Medicines Affect Your Bones? What a New Review Shows

social.instagram_caption:
"Will this medicine weaken my bones?" If that question has crossed your mind on a GLP-1 medicine, you're far from alone.

A new systematic review (Archives of Osteoporosis, Oct 23, 2026) pulled together 8 randomized trials, just 493 people in total, in adults with overweight or obesity (5 trials also included type 2 diabetes). The drugs tested were exenatide, liraglutide, semaglutide and dulaglutide. None of the trials tested tirzepatide.

The honest answer: certainty is very low. One semaglutide trial saw slightly lower spine and whole-body bone density. One liraglutide trial saw lower spine and hip density; another liraglutide trial saw no spine change. Not enough data yet to know what this means for fracture risk.

Worth knowing: weight loss itself, even from dieting alone, has been linked to a small drop in hip bone density in diet trials. Recommended general habits (not yet tested for bone on GLP-1 medicines): muscle-strengthening at least 2 days a week (CDC), starting gently, and protein food at each meal, unless your clinician has told you to limit protein.

Save this for your next appointment, and share it with someone who's asked this. Common side effects of GLP-1 medicines include stomach (GI) symptoms like nausea. Don't stop or change your medicines on your own.

#GLP1 #BoneHealth #Semaglutide #Liraglutide #MetabolicHealth

This content is for educational purposes only. Not personal advice. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

issues.problem: Without its scope, '0 trials' can read as 'no bone data on tirzepatide exists anywhere'. The review simply didn't include it. Also, tirzepatide is a dual GIP/GLP-1 agonist, so it was arguably outside the scope of a GLP-1 receptor agonist review.
issues.fix: Change value to "Not in this review" and body sentence to: "Tirzepatide was not included in this review."

issues.claim: another liraglutide trial showed no spine change
issues.problem: Reports of the review describe 'minimal' bone density changes with liraglutide 1.8 mg, not zero. 'No change' is slightly stronger than the source.
issues.fix: Replace with: "while another liraglutide trial (diabetes dose) showed little change."

issues.claim: One semaglutide trial (64 people) showed slightly lower spine and whole-body bone density
issues.problem: It doesn't name the comparator. The difference was measured against placebo.
issues.fix: "One semaglutide trial (64 people) showed slightly lower spine and whole-body bone density versus placebo"

issues.claim: Start gently / Build up at a comfortable pace
issues.problem: People with osteoporosis or a past fracture may need tailored exercise advice. The caveat is on slide 7 but not next to the tip itself.
issues.fix: Detail: "Build up slowly; ask your clinician first if you have osteoporosis"
